summary: Independent exact-SHA review of deployment-controller f9a51c05 found five blocking fail-closed gaps in the legacy pre-approval quarantine path; current tests pass but do not cover the risky activation-event and audit-state cases.
validation: Reviewer confirmed focused go test passes
blockers: Activation-event reconciliation does not require exactly one linked activation and can fall through to mutating normal reconciliation on missing/mismatched legacy state.
Legacy Work validation accepts nonterminal/unknown phases and can miss unexpected linked Work when repositoryDeploymentRef is nil.
Generation matching accepts generation 3+ instead of exact v0.6.4 Activate generation 2.
Referenced proof, issuance Lease, and Work deletion timestamps are not rejected.
High-risk activation-event, work-phase, deletion-timestamp, and generation-drift cases lack CRD/status-subresource coverage.
next_action: Remediate the five findings with exact fail-closed classifiers, zero-write mismatch behavior, and focused status-subresource tests, then commit and re-review the new exact SHA.

issues.title: Activation-event path can bypass exact linked-state validation
issues.details: Require a complete linked-activation list and exact name+UID match; missing or mismatched legacy request state must return a terminal zero-write error.

issues.title: Work terminal-state validation is incomplete
issues.details: Whitelist terminal legacy Work phases only and detect all unexpected linked Work, including nil repositoryDeploymentRef cases.

issues.title: Legacy Activate generation classifier is too broad
issues.details: Require Generation exactly 2 for the v0.6.4 Activate transition.

issues.title: Deleting audit objects are accepted
issues.details: Reject non-zero deletion timestamps on referenced proofs, issuance Leases, and linked Work before any write.

issues.title: Risky legacy migration cases lack integration-level coverage
issues.details: Add the strongest available CRD/status-subresource tests plus race coverage for duplicate/mismatch/missing activation-event state, Work phases, deletion timestamps, and generation drift.
